clue.text: Grindstone, spins with increasing speed

indicators.note: the word grindstone spins round, so its letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A grindstone whirls faster and faster as it is worked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spins' makes an anagram of GRINDSTONE; the result is the musical direction for gradually quickening tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical marking telling players to accelerate gradually, from Italian for tightening.

clue.text: Part of "South Pacific'"? Put a sock in it, somehow!

indicators.note: a and the punch go inside the jumbled pair of letters
the word it is jumbled somehow into a different order

parts.note: to sock is to hit, punch

explanation.surface: Someone at a performance of the musical South Pacific is told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put a sock in it' reads as a demand for silence; 'somehow' jumbles 'it' and 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A French Polynesian island, one part of the South Pacific ocean.

clue.text: Just starting a nice hot stew

indicators.note: the words a nice hot are stewed into a fresh mixture

explanation.surface: Someone is about to begin cooking a pleasant hot casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' makes an anagram of A NICE HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudimentary, only begun and not yet fully formed.

clue.text: Star-gazing after midnight requires such expert knowledge of tables

indicators.note: the study of the stars comes after the letter from midnight

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night
astronomy is scientific star-gazing

explanation.surface: Observing the stars late at night needs knowledge of mathematical tables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' gives G, the middle of NIGHT. 'tables' suggests astronomical charts but means dining tables.
explanation.definitionFit: The art and science of fine eating, knowledge of good food served at table.

clue.text: Fertilizer rank after dark, would you say?

indicators.note: the question asks how the phrase sounds when spoken

parts.note: a rank is a rate or grade, and after dark is night, giving a night rate

explanation.surface: A gardener asks whether a fertilizer smells foul at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' suggests a bad smell but is RATE; 'after dark' is NIGHT, and spoken the two sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt such as sodium nitrate, widely spread on fields as plant food.

clue.text: Lights etc left out for King of Mercia

indicators.note: the letter for left is left out of the word for the meats

parts.note: lights are lungs, and with other organ meats make up offal

explanation.surface: Lamps and such are omitted for an ancient English king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights' means animal lungs sold as butcher's meat, not lamps; OFFAL loses its L. Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: The 8th-century Mercian ruler famous for his dyke along the Welsh border.

clue.text: Deposit of ten cents sent round

indicators.note: the word sent goes round the coin

parts.note: a dime is a US coin worth ten cents

explanation.surface: A deposit of a few coins has been posted away.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid is a deposit.

clue.text: Puff-organ?

parts.note: not a wind instrument or lung but a newspaper that carries puffs, meaning promotional notices

explanation.walkthrough: A puff is a piece of promotion; many local newspapers carry a name meaning a publisher of such notices.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper title for a paper of notices, or anyone placing commercial promotion.

clue.text: Supporter of half-day closing

indicators.note: only half of the named weekday is kept, its second half dropped

parts.note: Friday stands for a day, an example of one
a closing is an end

explanation.surface: Someone backs the custom of shops shutting for half a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' with 'day' keeps FRI, the first half of FRIDAY; 'closing' is END.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally or backer is a supporter, as in a friend of the arts.

clue.text: First of 'spruce in copse is densely packed

indicators.note: the opening letter of spruce goes inside the word for a copse

parts.note: a thicket is a copse, a dense clump of trees

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word spruce is taken

explanation.surface: A spruce stands in a crowded copse of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocky and solidly built, or closely set, as in thickset hedges.

clue.text: A hitch may occur here, by the way

explanation.walkthrough: 'hitch' means a hitchhiker's thumbed lift, not a snag; 'by the way' is read literally as beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The verge of a road is where a hitchhiker thumbs a lift, and it lies literally beside the way.

clue.text: Prima donna near to Stradivari's heart

indicators.note: the letters sit in the middle part of the name Stradivari, close to its centre

explanation.surface: An opera star holds a Stradivarius violin dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near to ... heart' points to the letters just around the centre of STRADIVARI.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading female opera singer, celebrated and often temperamental.

clue.text: .Weakness of floor reported

annotationWithheld.why: Weakness of floor reported (10), answer DEFICIENCY: the scan prints this exactly; no homophone of a word for floor giving the answer could be found, and a search found no parse

clue.text: Travelling-case,.. square and accommodating?

parts.note: something square is old-fashioned, out of fashion, so out
accommodating and tolerant means patient

explanation.surface: A suitcase for travel is described as square and roomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling-case' is not luggage but a hospital case who travels in for treatment; 'square' means unfashionable, hence OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital patient who visits for treatment without staying overnight is a case who comes and goes.

clue.text: Scottish striker, perhaps, belonging to a university.

explanation.walkthrough: Hamilton Academical is a Scottish professional football team, nicknamed the Accies.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamilton Academical is a Scottish football club, so a forward could play for it; the adjective also means relating to a college or university.

clue.text: Filled with enthusiasm, go back and iron (using connection)

parts.note: to be fired up is to be filled with enthusiasm

indicators.note: the word go is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone eager is told to go back and press clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GO into OG. The bracketed 'using connection' signals that this iron is the one used in connection with a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron, a metal support for logs in a hearth, is an iron fireside implement.

clue.text: Contestant on' Cumbrian fells who never wins

explanation.walkthrough: Fell running is hill racing in Cumbria's Lake District, so the first reading is a racer going up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fell-race competitor climbs upwards on the Lake District hills; and the person placed second never takes first prize.

clue.text: Service bell?

parts.note: not a bell for calling a waiter but the hymn of a church service, which also names the bell rung at that point of Mass

explanation.definitionFit: The Holy, holy, holy hymn of the Mass gives its name to a small bell rung during the Eucharist.

clue.text: Deep-blue river rises, unpolluted all round

indicators.note: the word for unpolluted goes all round the reversed river

parts.note: clean means unpolluted

indicators.note: in a down clue the river reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A deep-blue river swells and stays free of pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rises' means read upwards, i.e. backwards; 'all round' signals that the word for unpolluted encloses the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A sky-coloured shade, a deep clear azure.

clue.text: No heart trouble for this unnamed player

indicators.note: the words no heart are troubled, stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cardiac all-clear is given to an anonymous sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' makes an anagram of NO HEART. A. N. Other is the stand-in name on a team sheet for a player not yet chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: The placeholder name used on a team list for an unspecified player.

clue.text: Vehicle in legal transfer

explanation.definitionFit: A carriage or other means of transport, and also the legal transfer of property title by deed.

clue.text: Stand up at -the back!

explanation.definitionFit: To rise up on hind legs, as a horse does; and the hindmost part or position.

clue.text: Bitter enough to turn a paper red

definitions.text: enough to turn a paper red

explanation.definitionFit: Sharp or sour in taste, and of a strength to redden blue litmus paper in a chemistry test.

clue.text: Keep on top of this pub trumpeter?

definitions.text: Keep on top of this pub trumpeter?

parts.words: Keep on top of this pub trumpeter?
parts.note: a keep is a castle, and a famous London pub name puts a castle with this trunked animal that trumpets

explanation.walkthrough: The Elephant and Castle is a London pub that gave its name to a district; its sign shows a castle on an elephant's back.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunked beast that trumpets, pictured on the pub sign carrying a castle.

clue.text: Egg on Lincoln Square

parts.note: Abe is the short name of President Abraham Lincoln
a T-square is a drawing tool, so a square gives T

explanation.surface: A crowd urges people on in a square named after Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage or incite someone, often in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Cooked enchilada left out in ranch-house

indicators.note: the word enchilada is cooked up into a new arrangement
the letter for left is taken out of the enchilada mix

explanation.surface: A Mexican dish is prepared without its leftovers in a ranch kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes L from ENCHILADA, leaving ENCHIADA, which 'Cooked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish-American estate or the main dwelling on a large ranch.

clue.text: Blow the French pair!

parts.note: a coup is a sudden blow or stroke
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance at a French couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things or people together, a twosome.

clue.text: Having injured trunk, elect to wear such a sweater

indicators.note: the words trunk and elect are injured, damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with a hurt torso chooses a particular jumper to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' makes an anagram of TRUNK plus ELECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumper with a high close-fitting rolled collar is this style of sweater.
